chunks: And from him, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Ali ibn al-Nu'man, from Umar ibn Yazid, from Jabir, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:

He was asked about Friday and its night, so he said: 'Its night is a bright night and its day is a radiant day; and there is no day on the face of the earth on which the sun sets more often than [a person is] spared from the Fire. Whoever dies on Friday, knowing the right of the People of this House, Allah writes for him a discharge from the Fire and a discharge from the punishment of the grave. And whoever dies on the night of Friday is freed from the Fire.'

key_terms.عَارِفًا بِحَقِّ أَهْلِ هَذَا الْبَيْتِ: Knowing the right/authority of the People of this House (Ahl al-Bayt)

ai.seo_question: What are the spiritual benefits and eschatological rewards for dying on Friday according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) elevates Friday as the preeminent day of the week, describing its night as 'bright' and its day as 'radiant,' emphasizing that the sun sets upon it more frequently than upon any other day. He links the spiritual status of the Ahl al-Bayt directly to eschatological deliverance, stating that those who die on Friday with recognized knowledge of their rights are granted exemption from the Fire and the punishment of the grave, while those who die on Friday night are freed from the Fire. This underscores the Shia theological principle that *ma'rifah* (gnosis/recognition) of the Imams is the key to salvation, transforming the temporal significance of the day into a permanent spiritual reality.
